memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These are the names of the sons of Israel who went to Egypt with Jacob, each with his family: Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah; Issachar, Zebulun and Benjamin; Dan and Naphtali; Gad and Asher." - Exodus 1:1-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Exodus opens the way a family album opens — with names. Not with battles or miracles, but with the names of ordinary men who once walked into Egypt with their father Jacob, looking for food during a famine.

Notice that God did not begin this book with statistics. He began with names. Reuben, who failed his father badly. Levi, who once took up the sword in anger. Judah, who had a shameful chapter in his own story. These were not polished men. Yet God wrote each name down, and He kept every one of them in His plan.

This is how our God works. He deals with people, not crowds. He knows the name of the son who wandered, the daughter who is tired, the parent who feels forgotten in a big city. When Jesus later said that the Shepherd calls His own sheep by name (Jn 10:3), He was showing us the same heart that opens Exodus.

Whatever your failures, your name is not lost to God. From Judah's line the Saviour Himself would come — proof that God can weave broken stories into His redemption.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God knows me personally, or only generally?
2. Which past failure makes me feel disqualified from God's plan?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You know me by name and have not written me off. Help me to live today as one who is truly seen and truly loved by You. Amen.
